condition.zh: 慢性病 · 長期鴉片類

title.en: Pain medicine: a multidisciplinary clinic day

tagline.zh: 一本疼痛日記、一支鼻噴劑、一位接生了半個鎮的奶奶
tagline.en: A pain diary, a nasal spray, and a grandma who delivered half the town

desc.zh: 今天沒有針、沒有 C 臂。你的工具是問題、時間，和一個願意一起慢慢來的計畫。
desc.en: No needles, no C-arm today. Your tools are questions, time and a plan that's willing to go slowly together.

desc.zh: 你聽的是痛背後的那些話：害怕、睡不著、被說「像老房子」的那一天。
desc.en: You listen for the words behind the pain: fear, sleeplessness, the day someone said 'your spine is like an old house'.

about.zh: 口頭禪：「分數不是目標，生活才是。」診間牆上貼的是病人畫的圖，不是證書。
about.en: Catchphrase: 'The score isn't the goal; life is.' The clinic wall shows drawings by patients, not certificates.

about.zh: 問問題的速度很慢，慢到病人會把真正的答案說出來。
about.en: Asks questions slowly, slowly enough that patients give the real answer.

about.zh: 背得出每一位病人的處方史。最常問的一句：「這個藥，還在幫你嗎？」
about.en: Knows every patient's prescribing history by heart. Her favourite question: 'Is this medicine still helping you?'

role.zh: 病人・56 歲前工地主任

about.zh: 多年前從鷹架摔下來，腰椎骨折固定後一直痛。鴉片類吃了好幾年，劑量一路往上，痛沒有少，生活越來越小。
about.en: Fell from scaffolding years ago; the lumbar fracture was fixed but the pain stayed. Several years on opioids, the dose creeping up, the pain no less, his life getting smaller.

about.zh: 上個月打電話來說他白天坐著就睡著。今天跟來，手上抓著一張寫滿問題的紙。
about.en: Phoned last month to say he falls asleep sitting up. Came along today clutching a page full of questions.

role.zh: 病人・79 歲退休助產士

about.zh: 接生了半個鎮的孩子，從不怕痛。去年長了皮蛇，好了以後，衣服碰到胸口就像火燒。
about.en: Delivered half the town's babies and never feared pain. Had shingles last year; since it healed, clothes touching her chest feel like fire.

about.zh: 大學生，當年也是奶奶接生的。手機裡有一張表，記著奶奶每晚醒來幾次。
about.en: A university student whom Grandma also delivered. Keeps a chart on her phone of how often Grandma wakes each night.

about.zh: 晚上的電話總是很短，但會把病人的問題原封不動轉達。
about.en: Night calls are always brief, but she passes on the patient's question word for word.

plain.zh: 持續超過組織正常癒合時間的痛。它不只是傷口的訊號，也和神經系統、睡眠、情緒、生活交纏在一起。
plain.en: Pain lasting beyond normal tissue healing. It is not just a signal from an injury; it is tangled up with the nervous system, sleep, mood and daily life.

plain.zh: 嗎啡一類的強效止痛藥。急性劇痛很有用，長期用在慢性疼痛效果常常越來越差，風險越來越多。
plain.en: Strong painkillers of the morphine family. Very useful for severe acute pain; used long term for chronic pain they often help less and less while the risks grow.

plain.zh: 依計畫慢慢降低藥量，速度和病人一起決定，可以暫停或調整。不是突然停藥。
plain.en: Lowering the dose slowly to a plan whose pace is agreed with the patient and can pause or change. Not stopping suddenly.

plain.zh: 長期使用後突然停藥，身體出現的反應：焦躁、流汗、腹瀉、疼痛加劇、失眠。
plain.en: The body's reaction when a long-used drug stops suddenly: agitation, sweating, diarrhoea, worse pain, insomnia.

term.zh: 鴉片類引起的痛覺過敏

plain.zh: 長期使用鴉片類後，神經系統反而對痛更敏感，加藥讓痛變得更廣、更難形容。
plain.en: After long opioid use the nervous system becomes more sensitive to pain, and raising the dose makes the pain spread and become harder to describe.

plain.zh: 會讓疼痛變成慢性的心理社會因素：怕動、災難化思考、憂鬱、工作與家庭的壓力。
plain.en: Psychosocial factors that push pain towards chronicity: fear of movement, catastrophising, low mood, work and family stress.

plain.zh: 把痛想成最壞的結果：「一定是脊椎壞掉了」「我這輩子完了」。這種想法本身會讓痛更大。
plain.en: Thinking of pain in worst-case terms: 'my spine must be broken', 'my life is over'. The thinking itself makes the pain bigger.

plain.zh: 每天固定做一段量的活動，好的日子不多做、壞的日子不完全不動，再慢慢往上加。
plain.en: A fixed amount of activity each day: not overdoing good days, not stopping on bad ones, and building up slowly.

plain.zh: 俗稱皮蛇的帶狀皰疹好了以後，受傷的神經持續痛。老人特別常見。
plain.en: Nerve pain that persists after shingles has healed. Especially common in older people.

plain.zh: 一條脊神經根負責感覺的那一片皮膚。帶狀皰疹沿著一個皮節走，所以是一側、一條帶子。
plain.en: The strip of skin supplied by one spinal nerve root. Shingles follows one dermatome, so it is one-sided and band-shaped.

plain.zh: 神經本身受傷造成的痛：燒灼、電擊、輕碰就痛。一般止痛藥效果差，要用神經痛的藥。
plain.en: Pain from damage to the nerves themselves: burning, electric, painful to light touch. Ordinary painkillers work poorly; nerve-pain medicines are used.

plain.zh: 常用的神經痛藥。會頭暈想睡；和鴉片類一起用，呼吸抑制的風險加乘。
plain.en: Common nerve-pain medicines. They cause dizziness and drowsiness; combined with opioids the risk of breathing suppression multiplies.

plain.zh: 能暫時逆轉鴉片類過量的鼻噴藥，家人在家就能用。用了還是要叫救護車，因為它的作用可能比鴉片類短。
plain.en: A nasal spray that temporarily reverses opioid overdose, usable by family at home. An ambulance is still needed, since it may wear off before the opioid does.

text.zh: 夾在手指上，告訴你血氧。可是它不會告訴你呼吸變慢了；那要你自己數。
text.en: Clips on a finger and tells you the oxygen level. It won't tell you breathing has slowed; you count that yourself.

text.zh: 小方的武器。查得到每一個門診開過什麼。阿忠的神經痛藥，原來另一個門診也開了一份。
text.en: Fang's weapon: it shows what every clinic has prescribed. Chung's nerve-pain tablets, it turned out, were also prescribed by another clinic.

text.zh: 醫師、心理師、藥師的名字排在一起。慢性疼痛沒有一個人能單獨治好。
text.en: Doctor, psychologist and pharmacist side by side. Nobody treats chronic pain alone.

text.zh: 記的不是分數，是今天走了多遠、睡了多久、有沒有跟孫子在公園坐一下。第一頁寫著：「巷口・報紙」。
text.en: It records not scores but how far he walked, how long he slept, whether he sat in the park with his grandson. Page one says: 'end of the lane, newspaper'.

text.zh: 阿忠嫂把它放在電視旁邊，全家都找得到。上午學怎麼用，下午差一點就用上。
text.en: Mrs Chung keeps it next to the television where the whole family can find it. Learned in the morning; nearly needed by the afternoon.

name.zh: 為什麼鴉片類越吃越沒用

text.zh: 長期使用會產生耐受，同樣的量效果變差；有些人還會出現鴉片類引起的痛覺過敏。副作用卻一直累積：嗜睡、跌倒、便秘、睡眠呼吸中止、荷爾蒙下降、情緒低落、過量風險。慢性疼痛的目標是功能與生活，不是把分數壓到零；運動治療、心理治療、睡眠與其他藥物，常比加量更有幫助。
text.en: Long-term use brings tolerance, so the same dose does less, and some people develop opioid-induced hyperalgesia. Meanwhile side effects pile up: drowsiness, falls, constipation, sleep apnoea, low hormones, low mood, overdose risk. In chronic pain the goal is function and life, not a score of zero; exercise therapy, psychological therapy, sleep and other medicines often help more than a higher dose.

text.zh: 慢慢來、一起決定、可以暫停；同時加上非藥物治療、處理睡眠與情緒；給家裡拮抗劑鼻噴劑，因為耐受下降後如果吃回原量更容易過量；固定追蹤，絕不放棄病人。突然停藥會戒斷、劇痛，有人因此轉向非法藥物，往往比繼續吃更危險。
text.en: Go slowly, decide together, allow pauses; add non-drug treatment and deal with sleep and mood; give naloxone for home, because once tolerance falls, going back to the old dose is likelier to cause overdose; follow up regularly and never abandon the patient. Stopping suddenly brings withdrawal and severe pain, drives some people to illicit drugs, and is often more dangerous than carrying on.

text.zh: 帶狀皰疹後神經痛是神經病變性疼痛，一般止痛藥效果差。老人用神經痛藥要從低開始、慢慢調，注意頭暈、跌倒與夜間起床；局部貼片的全身副作用少，是好選擇。最危險的是多個鎮靜性藥物疊在一起：鴉片類、加巴噴丁類、安眠藥，尤其有睡眠呼吸中止的人。
text.en: Post-herpetic neuralgia is neuropathic pain and responds poorly to ordinary painkillers. In older people nerve-pain medicines start low and go slow, watching for dizziness, falls and night-time trips to the toilet; topical patches have few whole-body effects and are a good option. The real danger is stacking sedating drugs: opioids, gabapentinoids, sleeping pills, especially with sleep apnoea.

note.zh: 今天：一個減量、一位奶奶
note.en: Today: a taper and a grandma

lines.zh: 今天兩位主角。阿忠，鴉片類吃了好幾年還是痛；楊奶奶，帶狀皰疹後神經痛，晚上睡不著。
lines.en: Two main characters today. Chung, years on opioids and still in pain; Grandma Yang, post-herpetic neuralgia, can't sleep at night.

lines.zh: 阿忠的劑量這兩年一路往上。另外，處方系統顯示別的門診也開了神經痛的藥給他。
lines.en: Chung's dose has climbed for two years. And the prescribing system shows another clinic is also giving him a nerve-pain medicine.

lines.zh: 分數不是目標，生活才是。今天先問他想要什麼樣的生活。
lines.en: The score isn't the goal; life is. Today we start by asking what life he wants.

lines.zh: 我準備了恐懼迴避和災難化思考的問卷，還有睡眠與情緒的量表。
lines.en: I've got the fear-avoidance and catastrophising questionnaires ready, plus sleep and mood scales.

lines.zh: 很好。這些黃旗，比片子更能預測他會不會好。
lines.en: Good. Those yellow flags predict recovery better than any scan.

note.zh: 阿忠：痛沒少，生活變小了
note.en: Chung: the pain hasn't shrunk, his life has

lines.zh: 我以前一個人帶整個工地，現在連走到巷口買報紙都不行。
lines.en: I used to run a whole building site. Now I can't walk to the end of the lane for a newspaper.

lines.zh: 他白天坐著就睡著，晚上打呼很大聲，有時候還停一下。
lines.en: He nods off sitting up in the daytime, snores loudly at night, and sometimes stops breathing for a moment.

lines.zh: 你怕動了會更糟嗎？
lines.en: Are you afraid moving will make it worse?

lines.zh: 怕。以前有醫生說我的脊椎「像老房子」。
lines.en: Yes. A doctor once told me my spine was 'like an old house'.

lines.zh: 這一句話，可能比骨折還傷人。
lines.en: That one sentence may have hurt more than the fracture.

lines.zh: 三年來，有人好好摸過他的背嗎？重新檢查。
lines.en: In three years, has anyone properly examined his back? Do it again.

post.zh: 左側薦髂關節壓痛，腰旁肌肉很緊，神經學正常。
post.en: Left sacroiliac joint tender, paraspinal muscles tight, neurology normal.

post.zh: 有一部分是機械性的痛，可以用運動治療處理，不一定要靠鴉片類。
post.en: Part of this is mechanical pain that exercise therapy can address; it needn't all fall on opioids.

lines.zh: 藥一直加，痛沒少。為什麼？
lines.en: The dose keeps rising and the pain doesn't fall. Why?

lines.zh: 耐受；還有鴉片類引起的痛覺過敏，身體反而對痛更敏感。
lines.en: Tolerance; and opioid-induced hyperalgesia, where the body becomes more sensitive to pain.

lines.zh: 副作用卻一直累積：嗜睡、跌倒、便秘、睡眠呼吸中止。他太太說的打呼停一下，你要記下來。
lines.en: Meanwhile side effects pile up: drowsiness, falls, constipation, sleep apnoea. Note what his wife said about the snoring pauses.

note.zh: 共同目標：走到巷口；慢慢減量
note.en: Shared goal: the end of the lane; a slow taper

lines.zh: 所以你們要把我的藥停掉？我會痛死。
lines.en: So you're going to stop my pills? The pain will kill me.

q.zh: 長期鴉片類、痛沒少、白天嗜睡。怎麼做？
q.en: Years of opioids, no less pain, daytime sleepiness. What now?

options.zh: 一起訂目標，慢慢減量，可隨時調整
options.en: Set goals together; taper slowly, adjustable

why.zh: 減量要慢、要討論、病人參與速度，同時加上運動、心理、睡眠的方法。目的是更安全、生活更大，不是處罰。
why.en: Tapering is slow, discussed, its pace shared with the patient, with exercise, psychological and sleep strategies alongside. The aim is safety and a bigger life, not punishment.

why.zh: 突然停藥會戒斷、劇痛、情緒崩潰，有人會轉去找非法藥物。突然停，常比繼續吃更危險。
why.en: Stopping suddenly brings withdrawal, severe pain and distress, and some people turn to illicit drugs. A sudden stop is often more dangerous than continuing.

options.en: Still in pain; raise the dose a bit

why.zh: 加了好幾年痛都沒少，再加只會增加嗜睡與過量的風險。
why.en: Years of increases haven't reduced the pain; more only adds drowsiness and overdose risk.

post.en: ...if it's slow, I'll give it a go.

lines.zh: 分數先放一邊。三個月後，你想做到什麼？
lines.en: Forget the score for now. In three months, what do you want to be able to do?

lines.zh: 自己走到巷口買報紙。帶孫子去公園坐一下。
lines.en: Walk to the end of the lane for my paper. Sit in the park with my grandson.

lines.zh: 那就用活動節奏：每天固定走一段，好的日子不多走，壞的日子也不完全不動。
lines.en: Then we use pacing: the same walk every day, no extra on good days, not nothing on bad ones.

post.zh: 這本疼痛日記，記的不是分數，是你走了多遠。
post.en: This pain diary records not scores but how far you walked.

lines.zh: 減量時風險會變：耐受下降後，萬一又吃回原來的量，更容易過量。家裡要放一支拮抗劑鼻噴劑。
lines.en: Tapering changes the risk: once tolerance drops, going back to the old dose is likelier to cause overdose. Keep a naloxone nasal spray at home.

lines.zh: 我要怎麼用？
lines.en: How do I use it?

q.zh: 家人發現他叫不醒，正確的順序？
q.en: Family find him unrousable: the right order?

steps.zh: 大聲叫名字、用力搓胸骨
steps.en: Shout his name, rub the breastbone hard

steps.zh: 依說明噴拮抗劑鼻噴劑
steps.en: Give the naloxone spray as instructed
Roll him into the recovery position

steps.zh: 仍沒反應，依說明再給一次

steps.en: Stay with him until help arrives

post.zh: 我會放在電視旁邊，誰都找得到。
post.en: I'll keep it by the TV where anyone can find it.

post.zh: 另外，另一個門診開的神經痛藥，我們統一由這裡開，不要兩份。
post.en: And the nerve-pain tablets from the other clinic: we'll prescribe them from here only, not two lots.

note.zh: 楊奶奶：帶狀皰疹後神經痛

lines.zh: 我接生了半個鎮的孩子，從來沒怕過痛。可是這個痛，衣服碰到就像火燒。
lines.en: I've delivered half this town and never feared pain. But this one: a blouse touches me and it's fire.

lines.zh: 去年長皮蛇，好了以後一直痛。我記了，她一個晚上醒好幾次。
lines.en: She had shingles last year and it's hurt ever since it healed. I've been keeping count: she wakes several times a night.

lines.zh: 右側胸口到背後一條帶子，輕輕碰就痛。
lines.en: A band from the right chest round to the back; light touch hurts.

question.zh: 右胸到背後一條單側、不過中線的帶狀皮膚，有舊疤與色素沉著，輕觸就劇痛。這是什麼？為什麼痛的形狀是一條帶子？
question.en: A one-sided band of skin from the right chest to the back, not crossing the midline, with old scars and pigmentation; light touch is agony. What is it, and why is the pain shaped like a band?

answer.zh: 帶狀皰疹後神經痛。水痘病毒潛伏在一條神經根，再活化時沿著那條神經的皮節發作，所以是一側、一條帶子、不過中線。皮疹好了，受傷的神經仍持續發出錯誤的痛訊號，是神經病變性疼痛：燒灼、電擊感、輕觸就痛。
answer.en: Post-herpetic neuralgia. The chickenpox virus lies dormant in one nerve root and, when reactivated, flares along that nerve's dermatome: one side, one band, not crossing the midline. After the rash heals the damaged nerve keeps sending false pain signals: neuropathic pain, burning, electric, painful to light touch.

post.zh: 一條帶子……難怪像被繩子綁住。
post.en: A band... no wonder it feels like I'm tied with rope.

guide.en: What kind of pain is this?

lines.zh: 傷害性的痛和神經病變性疼痛，治療一樣嗎？
lines.en: Is nociceptive pain treated the same as neuropathic pain?

lines.zh: 不一樣。神經痛對一般止痛藥反應差，要用神經痛的藥，例如加巴噴丁類，或局部貼片。
lines.en: No. Nerve pain responds poorly to ordinary painkillers; it needs nerve-pain medicines such as gabapentinoids, or a topical patch.

lines.zh: 她七十九歲。
lines.en: She's seventy-nine.

lines.zh: 從低開始、慢慢調，注意頭暈和晚上起床跌倒。先試局部貼片，全身副作用少。
lines.en: Start low, go slow, watch for dizziness and night-time falls. Try the topical patch first; fewer whole-body effects.

post.zh: 從低開始、慢慢來。跟接生一樣，急不得。
post.en: Start low, go slow. Like a delivery: you can't hurry it.

note.zh: 候診區叫不醒：鴉片類加神經痛藥
note.en: Unrousable in the waiting area: opioid plus nerve-pain drug

guide.en: Someone won't wake in the waiting area

lines.zh: 醫生！他等領藥的時候睡著了，叫不太醒，嘴唇有點紫！
lines.en: Doctor! He fell asleep waiting for his prescription and I can barely wake him. His lips look blue!

lines.zh: 他今天早上吃了什麼？
lines.en: What did he take this morning?

lines.zh: 他說今天要看醫生很緊張，多吃了一顆……還有另一個門診的神經痛藥。
lines.en: He was nervous about today, so he took an extra one... and the nerve-pain tablet from the other clinic.

lines.zh: 血氧往下掉，呼吸又慢又淺，打呼聲停了一下。
lines.en: Saturation is falling; breathing slow and shallow; the snoring stops for a moment.

options.zh: 叫人、刺激、暢通呼吸道、給氧
options.en: Call for help, stimulate, open the airway, oxygen

why.zh: 鴉片類加上加巴噴丁類與睡眠呼吸中止，呼吸抑制會加乘。叫人、刺激、暢通呼吸道、給氧；叫不醒或呼吸太慢就依規範給拮抗劑，並持續觀察。
why.en: Opioids plus gabapentinoids plus sleep apnoea multiply respiratory depression. Call for help, stimulate, open the airway, give oxygen; if he won't rouse or breathes too slowly, give naloxone per protocol and keep watching.

options.en: Let him sleep; he's just tired

why.zh: 「睡得很熟」是呼吸抑制最常見的偽裝。數呼吸、看血氧、叫醒他。
why.en: 'Sleeping soundly' is respiratory depression's commonest disguise. Count breaths, check saturation, wake him.

why.zh: 氧氣拉得高血氧，卻掩蓋了呼吸變慢與二氧化碳上升。要刺激、評估、備拮抗劑。
why.en: Oxygen lifts the saturation but hides slowing breaths and rising carbon dioxide. Stimulate, assess, have naloxone ready.

post.zh: 刺激之後他醒了，呼吸變快，血氧回來。拮抗劑在旁邊備著。
post.en: He's rousing with stimulation, breathing faster, saturation recovering. Naloxone is standing by.

post.zh: 多吃的一顆，加上神經痛藥，加上睡眠呼吸中止。就是這個組合。
post.en: One extra tablet, plus the nerve-pain drug, plus sleep apnoea. That's the combination.

post.zh: 上午才教他太太用鼻噴劑，下午就差點用上。送急診觀察，拮抗劑可能比藥效先退。
post.en: We taught his wife the spray this morning and nearly needed it this afternoon. ER for observation; naloxone can wear off before the drug does.

note.zh: 減量計畫加睡眠檢查；處方統一
note.en: Taper plan, sleep study, one prescriber

lines.zh: 今天差一點。也因為差一點，阿忠和他太太都懂了為什麼要減。
lines.en: Today was close. And because it was close, Chung and his wife now understand why we're tapering.

lines.zh: 他在急診跟我說：「我不想再讓我太太嚇成那樣。」這是最好的動機。
lines.en: In the ER he told me: 'I never want to frighten my wife like that again.' That's the best motivation there is.

lines.zh: 減量計畫加上睡眠檢查。神經痛的藥由我們統一開，不要兩個門診各開一份。
lines.en: Taper plan plus a sleep study. Nerve-pain medicine from us only, not one lot from each clinic.

lines.zh: 還有楊奶奶：老人的神經痛，從低開始、慢慢來，還要問她晚上起來會不會頭暈。
lines.en: And Grandma Yang: in older people, nerve pain means start low, go slow, and ask whether she's dizzy getting up at night.

note.zh: 阿忠回家；楊奶奶睡著了
note.en: Chung goes home; Grandma Yang sleeps

sub.zh: 「阿忠觀察完了，他問早上的計畫還算數嗎」
sub.en: 'Chung's observation is done; he asks if this morning's plan stands'

lines.zh: 阿忠觀察了幾個小時，清醒、呼吸正常，可以回家。他問：早上說的計畫還算數嗎？
lines.en: Chung has been observed for several hours: alert, breathing normally, fit for home. He asks: does this morning's plan still stand?

lines.zh: 算數。明天開始照計畫的第一步，慢慢來。鼻噴劑帶回家。
lines.en: It stands. Step one of the plan from tomorrow, slowly. The spray goes home with him.

lines.zh: 他太太說，已經放在電視旁邊了。
lines.en: His wife says it's already by the TV.

lines.zh: 他說你早上叫他今天全部停，他很怕今晚會戒斷，問可不可以不要停。
lines.en: He says you told him this morning to stop everything today. He's scared of withdrawal tonight and asks if he really must.

lines.zh: 我改計畫：不突然停。明天回門診，一起訂慢慢減的步驟。突然停，常比繼續吃更危險。
lines.en: I'm changing the plan: no sudden stop. Back to clinic tomorrow to agree a slow taper together. A sudden stop is often more dangerous than carrying on.

lines.zh: 早上我還想幫他加藥……今天下午證明了，那只會讓他更危險。
lines.en: This morning I wanted to raise his dose... this afternoon proved that would only make him less safe.

lines.zh: 不加。明天回門診，一起訂慢慢減的計畫，鼻噴劑帶回家。
lines.en: No increase. Back to clinic tomorrow to agree a slow taper together, and the spray goes home with him.

sub.en: 'Grandma has her patch on and she's asleep'

lines.zh: 醫生，奶奶第一次貼貼片，現在睡著了，起來上廁所也沒有頭暈。她說：謝謝你們慢慢來。
lines.en: Doctor, Grandma's first night with the patch: she's asleep, and no dizziness when she got up for the toilet. She says thank you for going slowly.

lines.zh: 分數不是目標，生活才是。今晚，一個人睡著了，一個人回家了。
lines.en: The score isn't the goal; life is. Tonight one person is asleep and another is home.

sub.zh: 分數不是目標，生活才是
sub.en: The score isn't the goal; life is
